entries.text: Hi, it's Mia from Replogle Globes. Thanks for taking a few minutes with me: your code, $20 off, shows up on screen as soon as we finish. What brings you to Replogle Globes today?
I'm looking to buy a globe.
Nice, a globe. Is it for you, or is it a gift for someone?
It's a gift for my child.
That's lovely. How old is your child, and what's the occasion?
He is turning four.
Four is a fun age, happy early birthday to him. What do you imagine him doing with the globe once he has it?
Just exploring all that you can see on it and the different countries. And where they are.
Exploring where everything is, that sounds like a great way to learn. What matters most to you when choosing it?
Price and size and accuracy.
Thank you.
You're welcome. Is there anything that would make you buy today, or anything holding you back?
Nothing in particular. I'm just looking for, um, an accurate glow based on a reputable seller that I can really rely on, and the cost is not too expensive, and the size not too big.
A reliable seller, fair price, and a manageable size, that makes sense. How did you find Replogle Globes?

I did a Google search, and it was on a couple different companies but then I noted that Replope go has a really good reputation online. And so I went to your website, and that's how I found your company.
Good to hear the reputation helped. Thinking about your son, what have you bought for him before that he really took to?

A lot of open ended toys and things that can curiosity, things that he can spend quite a lot of time on. Just explore and create and see what there is to learn from it, which is why I think a globe would be such a good gift because allows a lot of open ended thought and without much additional guidance.
That makes sense, a globe lets him wonder on his own. Is there anything you pay for regularly for him, and what keeps you coming back to it?
No. There's not anything we pay for regularly, but there what... There... We would if there was something available, but there's not.
That's good to know. What would that something look like for you, if it existed?
Um, I'm not sure. Probably something that provided open ended activities. Something that was novel and unique. Something that would allow for open ended and unstructured playtime,
especially independent play.
Independent play, got it. Roughly how much have you spent on toys like that for him over the past year?
I would say maybe a few hundred dollars
We don't need to spend too much on toys, thankfully. As we get a lot of gifts handed down or other toys passed down from um, other children that we know.
Handed down toys are a nice way to do it. And what would make a globe feel accurate and trustworthy to you?
I would... I'm looking for a globe that has accurate representations of all the countries and then also accurate sizing of different continents so that there's no skewed or biased data.
A globe shows true continent sizes, so it avoids the skew flat maps have. The product page has the exact details. Thanks again for your time: your code is coming up on your screen now. Goodbye!
